summary: Intro discovery call focused on Redwood deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and Helix's security requirements: SOC 2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, and data retention. AE + SE clarified hosted isolation and customer-managed KMS options; security architect flagged data residency and log retention constraints for EU regulated customers. Agreed next steps: share compliance artifacts, SAML guide, schedule SE deep dive.
topics: SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 compliance
SSO / SAML integration and IdP metadata
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm maya from Redwood, joining me is jordan, our senior se. how's everyone doing?
[00:05] Evan: Good, thanks. we have priya and tom on from infra/security. we wanted to run through your security posture — especially how hosted compares to dedicated/private for regulated finance data.
[00:15] Jordan: great, we'll cover compliance artifacts, sso, rbac, audit logs, encryption and data residency. quick note, i'll probably ask for your current infra layout during the call.
[00:28] Priya: perfect — quick context, Helix stores sanitized transactional metadata for analytics, but certain EU customers require strict residency and 7+ year retention for audit trails. we also have an internal rule for customer managed keys for sensitive PII.
[00:40] Tom: and we run in multi-cloud — gcp primary, aws secondary, some on prem for specific services. so network egress and VPC peering questions will matter.
[00:50] Maya: understood. first, compliance: we are SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 — we can share the reports, and hosted offering has those certifications centrally. dedicated also runs under our compliance umbrella but with additional isolation controls, and private (vpc / on-prem) gives you the most control for contractual needs.
[01:05] Priya: when you say dedicated "runs under your compliance umbrella," does that mean our data is still on Redwood-managed infrastructure but isolated? or do we get dedicated tenancy?
[01:14] Jordan: good q — dedicated is reserved GPU pools and isolated tenant slices within our infra. it's single-tenant for compute, network isolation via private subnets and strict ACLs, but the control plane remains Redwood-managed unless you choose Private which is customer-managed control plane. sorry if that was wordy.
[01:30] Evan: okay and private would be full control: customer runs the control plane in their VPC or on prem?
[01:36] Jordan: yes private deploys a control plane in your VPC -- you can opt for on-prem package too. in that model you control keys, networking, and we provide the orchestration package.
[01:45] Priya: important for us: key management. we prefer customer-managed keys (BYOK) with HSM-backed KMS. does redwood support CMKs and key rotation policies?
[01:55] Maya: yes, we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integrations (aws kms, gcp cloud kms) and we can support HSM-backed keys in Private deployments. for Hosted we can offer a bring-your-own-key flow where keys are in your cloud project and we get access via IAM roles, so we never persist raw key material.
[02:12] Tom: and is there support for rotating keys without downtime for cached kvs? I'm worried about cache invalidation during rotation and cold-start costs.
[02:21] Jordan: good point — our runtime supports key rotation patterns and we have KV cache rewrap flows; rotation requires a short rewrap step but not full model cache invalidation. we can run a rotation test during a pilot.
[02:35] Priya: auditability: we need immutable audit logs for all admin actions, key access events, and model rollouts. retention needs to be pluggable — by default 90 days but for regs we need 7 years or exportable logs.
[02:49] Maya: default log retention for hosted is 90 days in our console, with extended retention add-ons. we can export logs to your splunk/cloudwatch/gcs bucket for long-term retention — that's common for enterprise customers.
[02:59] Evan: are logs tamper-evident? chain-of-custody? we may need signed logs for some audits.
[03:06] Jordan: we don't provide a signed-log chain-of-custody by default in hosted, but in Dedicated/Private we can enable append-only write patterns and forward logs to your customer-controlled storage where you can implement immutability/retention with object locks. we also produce detailed access logs and admin audit trails in the console.
[03:25] Priya: ok — SSO: we run SAML 2.0 — integration needs to enforce group-based RBAC and SCIM provisioning ideally. is SCIM supported?
[03:33] Maya: yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. Jordan will send an integration guide and example metadata. roles sync via SCIM maps to our RBAC model so you can granularly map groups to roles.
[03:45] Jordan: to add: our RBAC supports least-privilege roles, custom roles, and token-level restrictions for actions like model deploy, rollback, or billing. you can also create service accounts with granular scopes.
[03:58] Tom: do you have separation between billing and infra ops? we don't want billing team to see model prompts or logs.
[04:05] Jordan: yes we have role scoping; billing-only roles can see cost dashboards without access to prompt content or raw logs. raw transcripts and prompt contents are protected by redaction rules and access controls.
[04:18] Priya: encryption at rest — is all customer data encrypted? what about embeddings and cache?
[04:24] Maya: all persisted customer data is encrypted at rest using storage-level encryption; for hosted we use provider-managed disk encryption unless you enable customer-managed keys. KV cache and embeddings at rest are encrypted; in-memory KVs are protected in our runtime and not persisted unless configured.
[04:40] Evan: what about egress and data residency — we have EU customers that contractually require data not to leave eu, and keys stored in eu kms. can hosted keep data in eu region?
[04:50] Jordan: yes, hosted operates in multiple regions; you can pin requests to eu regions. for strict residency we often recommend Dedicated in-region or Private deploy so keys and data never leave your VPC.
[05:02] Priya: for contract language we also need obligations around data deletion and proof of deletion. do you provide deletion certificates or logs showing data purge?
[05:12] Maya: we can provide deletion logs and show object lifecycle transitions; for Private, deletion is in your control. for hosted we can provide attestations and a deletion pipeline that emits logs to your storage. we'll follow up with exact language.
[05:24] Tom: network isolation on dedicated: do you support private peering and no public egress? we want to avoid any public endpoints for model traffic.
[05:33] Jordan: Dedicated supports private peering and static private IPs; you can disable internet egress for inference nodes and use NAT for control plane comms if needed. Private deployment removes Redwood-managed control plane exposure entirely.
[05:47] Priya: incident response: can we get details on your IR process, MTTD/MTTR, and notification windows? also pen test cadence and third-party attestations?
[05:58] Maya: our SOC2 report includes IR overview; we do quarterly tabletop exercises, we publish MTTD/MTTR SLAs for enterprise contracts, and we run annual pen tests plus periodic external scans. we can share the pen test summary redacted.
[06:13] Evan: threat model: do you allow us to run our own pen tests against dedicated or private? and do you require a scope or waiver?
[06:21] Jordan: for Dedicated we have a coordinated testing program — you can run tests with a standard authorization and scope; for Private you run them in your environment. we'll provide the standard pen test process doc.
[06:33] Priya: data retention policy details: our compliance team wants to set data retention per-customer and per-environment, especially for logs and prompt traces. can that be configured per-tenant?
[06:44] Jordan: yes, retention policies can be configured per-tenant; hosted has defaults, but for enterprise we can set per-tenant retention and export pipelines to your storage for longer-term retention.
[06:56] Tom: curious about model caching — is cached KV data considered persistent and subject to our retention rules?
[07:03] Jordan: cached KV keys are treated as derivable state; we persist caches for performance but they can be configured to not persist to long-term storage. we can align that with your retention policies and scrub caches upon request.
[07:17] Priya: regulatory concern: proof of sub-processor list and where data is processed; need a full subprocessing map including cloud region endpoints.
[07:26] Maya: we'll share our subprocessors and region map — the SOC2 artifact and our data processing addendum list that. we'll send the latest list as part of the security packet.
[07:38] Evan: what about ML model provenance and third-party models? if I pick an open model via redwood, where is the model hosted and is inference done inside our region?
[07:48] Jordan: models are hosted in region when available; if a model variant isn't available in-region we fall back to a compatible variant or route cross-region with customer consent — you can lock to region-only policies to avoid cross-region calls.
[07:59] Priya: regarding change control, when you push runtime updates or model upgrades, do you notify customers and offer canary windows?
[08:08] Maya: yes, release notes, canary deploys, and rollback hooks are standard. for enterprise we contract notice periods for planned maintenance.
[08:18] Tom: encryption key access logging — do you emit KMS access events into logs we can retain?
[08:24] Jordan: yes, when using customer-managed keys in your KMS, the KMS logs show every crypto op; we also emit operational events into our audit logs that can be forwarded to you.
[08:35] Priya: curious about a small technical detail: token-level redaction and PII extraction — is there a built-in redaction pipeline before data is stored?
[08:44] Jordan: we offer optional built-in redaction and PII scrubbing filters; however for full control many customers run a pre-processing layer in their environment to scrub sensitive fields before sending. we can provide reference patterns.
[08:57] Evan: can we do a pilot where we test rotation, SSO, and retention for a small workload? timeline: we'd like results in ~2 weeks.
[09:05] Maya: yes — we suggested a 2-week pilot. Jordan: we'll scope the pilot to include SAML SSO, a small dedicated pool or hosted in-eu region, KMS rotation test, and log export.
[09:18] Priya: ok about licensing: we will need contract clauses for data residency, deletion attestations, and ability to audit. is that standard?
[09:25] Maya: we have enterprise contract templates with those clauses; legal will work with you on required language.
[09:32] Tom: one more: do you provide per-token cost breakdown and cost allocation for multi-tenant usage so billing team can allocate costs across lines of business?
[09:40] Jordan: yes, console has token-level cost and per-route breakdowns; you can integrate billing export to your billing system.
[09:48] Evan: anything else we should prepare for the deep dive? Priya: i want to walk through our current KMS and IdP metadata.
[09:56] Maya: perfect. we'll send the security packet today and schedule the deep dive.
[10:00] -- transcript continues with detailed technical clarifications and a short Q&A between 10:00 and 30:00 minutes, including Jordan describing the KMS rewrap flow, sample SCIM mapping table, and examples of audit log JSON fields. some phrases transcribed imperfectly: "KV cache" heard as "k-v case", "append-only" as "append tone".
[20:12] Jordan: ...so in the rewrap flow we pull the cached key, call the kms rewrap api, rotate the wrapping key, and then update the cache pointer; the operation is designed to avoid full cache invalidation.
[24:30] Priya: can you also include a note about retention for model prompt traces — we need a legal-safe retention that strips PII after 30 days unless escrowed by contract.
[24:45] Maya: yes we can document that.
[28:03] Evan: last question on attestation — do you provide a mechanism for us to request an on-site security review or shared penetration test results for enterprise deals?
[28:12] Maya: yes enterprise agreements can include a clause for shared pen test summaries and an on-site review with proper NDAs.
[28:22] Tom: cool, thanks.
[28:25] Maya: recap: we'll share SOC2/ISO, subprocessors, SAML guide, SCIM examples, pen test summary, and a pilot scope. action items assigned. schedule deep dive for Nov 3.
[28:40] Evan: thanks everyone.
[28:43] Priya: thanks.
[28:45] (call ends)
